messages:

Subject: Sudden request queueing in us-west — are you seeing this?

Sean,

We started seeing a spike in request queuing from our us-west traffic at ~07:50 PT — latency jumps to p95 ~1.8s and a subset of requests return 502/504. It's affecting our chat agents and leading to retries. Our SRE pulled a couple of sampler traces and attached a short log snippet. Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing increased queueing or if this looks like something on our side?

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Maya Singh <maya@catalyst.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden request queueing in us-west — are you seeing this?

Hi Raj — thanks for the heads up and for the log snippet. We are seeing elevated queue lengths and p95 increases for a subset of us-west pools starting ~07:45 PT; engineering is looking into cause.

Immediate actions we have taken:
- Opened an incident (RI-20261118-queueing) and activated on-call.
- Initiated a regional reroute to fallback pools in us-east for affected routing keys — this should reduce queueing within the next 15–30 min for routed traffic.
- Asking SRE to collect producer/consumer metrics and KV-cache eviction traces; I've attached the runbook we're using.

I'm cc'ing Laura (infra on-call) and Marissa (customer ops) who will coordinate updates. We'll post to the public status page and share timeframe for remediation.

Status link: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/RI-20261118-queueing

I'll follow up with a concrete ETA as soon as we have more detail.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:35:00Z
Subject: Internal: investigating us-west queueing spike (incident RI-20261118-queueing)

Team,

Summary of findings so far (ETA 2h):
- Observable: sustained queue length increase on us-west pool A and elevated kv-cache churn coincident with a routing fanout spike around 07:40–08:00 PT. Some requests were retried by CatalystAI which amplified load.
- Immediate mitigation: exercised regional reroute for impacted routing keys to us-east pools; traffic has started moving but we are still seeing residual queueing for in-flight sessions pinned to the affected pool.
- Suspected cause: a combination of a routing fanout from a customer batch job + cache eviction leading to longer per-token compute.

Actions required:
1) Confirm CatalystAI's retry policy and whether they can temporarily reduce client-side retries for ~1 hour (helps backpressure).
2) Increase concurrency on fallback us-east pools (manual scale) — Marissa/Kim coordinate.
3) Capture and share per-route KV cache eviction logs and token-level timings (I've attached the runbook and a small excerpt).

Attachments referenced: regional-reroute-runbook.pdf; support-log-snippet.txt

I'll push a statuspage update once we have confirmation that the reroute reduced error rates.

Laura Bennett
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2026-11-18T14:02:00Z
Subject: Update: us-west queueing incident — reroute active and error rates improved

Raj / Maya,

Quick update following our actions this morning:
- What we changed: we activated a targeted regional reroute for the impacted routing keys and scaled the fallback us-east pools.
- Observed impact: error rate for your affected endpoints dropped from ~2.3% to ~0.2%; p95 latency improved from ~1.8s to ~0.45s for rerouted traffic.
- Current status: reroute remains active while we continue to drain pinned sessions on the original pool. No customer data was exposed; this was a capacity/routing and cache churn issue.

Next steps:
- Engineering will complete a post-incident RCA and share a timeline for permanent remediation (config changes + potential autoscaling rule adjustments). We expect the RCA within 72 hours.
- We'll publish a concise postmortem on the status page and share the link here.
- Request: if you can temporarily reduce client-side retry aggressiveness for the next 60 minutes it will reduce pressure while drains complete.

I've attached the runbook we referenced and the minimal log excerpt you provided.

Attachments: regional-reroute-runbook.pdf; support-log-snippet.txt
